JavaScript Fundamentals • Functions as values

Functions, const, Callbacks, and Why JavaScript Lets You Pass Behavior Around

JavaScript gets much easier when you stop thinking of a function as only “a block of code with a name” and start seeing it as a value. A function can be declared, stored in a variable, stored on an object, passed into another function, returned from a function, and even replaced at runtime. Every code example on this page is editable and runnable directly in the browser.

function declarations const function expressions arrow functions callbacks methods hoisting first-class functions
1 • What is a function?

A function is reusable behavior you can call later.

A function can receive input through parameters, do some work, and optionally return a value.

Editable example: greet()
Output
Press Run.

Parameters vs arguments

  • name is the parameter, the variable that receives input.
  • "Alice" is the argument, the actual value passed in.
  • return sends a value back to the caller.
  • After the function is defined, you can call it as many times as you want.
Quiz alertA parameter is in the function definition. An argument is the value supplied when the function is called.
2 • Traditional function declarations

The clearest form for beginners is often function name(...) {...}.

Function declarations have a special behavior called hoisting: the declaration is available before its physical location in the source file.

Hoisting works here
Output
Press Run.

Why this style is useful for teaching

function describeOutcome(...) {} reads almost like English: “define a function named describeOutcome.”

For named business operations such as validateUser, calculateTotal, or isLockedOut, this style is explicit and easy to scan.

3 • Functions stored in const

const can hold a function just like it can hold a string, number, or object.

This is called a function expression. JavaScript creates a function value, then stores that function value in a variable.

Function expression stored in const
Output
Press Run.

What const does and does not mean

const means the variable name cannot be reassigned to another value.

It does not mean the function is special, magical, frozen, or faster. It just means the variable reference stays fixed.

ImportantA function declaration is hoisted. A function expression assigned to const is not usable before the variable is initialized.

Why this fails

The variable sayHello exists in the scope, but it has not been initialized when the first line tries to call it. That is why this form behaves differently from a function declaration.

4 • Arrow functions

Arrow functions are shorter function expressions.

They are extremely common for small callbacks, especially inside map, filter, find, Promises, and event handlers.

Arrow function syntax
Output
Press Run.

Declaration vs expression vs arrow

FormExampleHoisted?Good fit
Function declarationfunction add(a,b) {...}YesNamed operations
Function expressionconst add = function(a,b) {...}NoFunctions stored as values
Arrow functionconst add = (a,b) => a+bNoShort callbacks
Arrow functions also do not create their own this. That matters later when objects and classes depend on this.
5 • Passing functions as parameters

JavaScript can pass behavior into another function.

Because functions are values, a function can be passed as an argument. The receiving function can call it later. That passed function is commonly called a callback.

Named callback passed as an argument
Output
Press Run. Notice the order.

Read the call from right to left

verifyCredentialsCallback("alice", handleVerification)

  1. "alice" is normal data.
  2. handleVerification is a function value.
  3. The verification function receives both.
  4. Later, it calls handleVerification(...).
Quiz alertA callback is not a special JavaScript API type. It is simply a function passed somewhere so another piece of code can call it later.

6 • Array methods use callbacks constantly

filter() does not require arrow functions.

The arrow syntax is common because it is compact, but a traditional named function works too.

This is why arrow functions became so popular. They are especially convenient for tiny functions passed into methods such as filter(), map(), and find().
7 • Methods on objects

A method is just a function stored on an object property.

The syntax feels special because you call it with a dot, but underneath, the property value is still a function.

Object method
Output
Press Run.

Why this matters

robot.speak refers to a function value. robot.speak() calls that function.

This distinction is important because you can pass the function around:

const action = robot.speak;

Now action also refers to that function.

8 • Weird but educational runtime reassignment

An object method can be replaced with a completely different function.

This looks strange at first, but it proves that methods are ordinary function values stored in properties.

Why const does not stop this
Output

Key distinctionconst robot = ... prevents reassigning the variable robot. It does not freeze all properties inside the object. The speak property can still be changed unless the object is deliberately frozen.
9 • Functions can even return functions

Functions are first-class values.

Passing a function into another function is only half the story. A function can also create and return a new function.

Return a function
Output
Press Run.

“First-class function” means...

  • Store a function in a variable.
  • Put a function in an object property.
  • Pass a function into another function.
  • Return a function from another function.

This is the foundation for callbacks, array methods, event handlers, Promises, and much of modern JavaScript.

10 • Which style should I use?

Use the style that communicates the job clearly.

SituationGood choiceWhy
Named business operationfunction validateUser(...) {}Very explicit and hoisted.
Short callback in filter()item => conditionCompact and extremely common.
Function stored in a variableconst fn = function(...) {}Makes the “function is a value” idea obvious.
Object behaviorobj.method()Natural for behavior associated with an object.
Need dynamic thisTraditional function/methodArrow functions inherit this instead of defining their own.
